description.narrative: By financing the development of shore power infrastructure at JNPA, enabling vessels to switch from auxiliary engines powered by heavy fuel oil to electricity while at berth, the project is expected to reduce GHG emissions and improve air quality in the surrounding areas. Additionally, the project is expected to showcase the large-scale viability of shore power adoption and its potential for replication across Indian ports, thereby promoting long-term sustainability in the maritime transport sector.

The proposed investment is A loan of up to US$70 million to Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) to be utilized towards capex for creation of shore power infrastructure at the port in two phases over next 2-3 years. The proposed project involves the installation and operation of shore power infrastructure (also known as cold ironing) at an existing commercial port terminal at JNPA in India. The project will include construction of 33kv substations, cable systems, e-house, frequency converters, and onshore power cape point connections at multiple berths. The system will enable docked vessels to plug into land-based electricity sources, allowing them to shut down their diesel auxiliary engines while at berth. The project aims to reduce air emissions (including SOx, NOx, and PM) and greenhouse gases (GHGs), improve local air quality, and contribute to decarbonization of maritime operations. This initiative aligns with the recommendations of the Green Port Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Ports Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Government of India (GoI). JNPA proposes to implement the project in phases across all terminals, engaging an EPC contractor for construction and maintenance (35 years) and Terminal Operators for operational responsibilities. . The first phase of the project will focus on one of the container terminal and Phase 2 will cover remaining terminals at JNPA
